stories.headline: Brazil's Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly leaves the country after losing
body: Media reports say Senator Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil after losing the presidential runoff to Lula.
The US says it will grant visas to him and his family.
A day earlier, Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to hand over his passports in a money laundering probe; he denies wrongdoing.
stories.joke: Lost an election, found a boarding pass.
stories.vc: Political drama after the vote keeps Brazil's currency jumpy, though a settled result helps longer-term investors.

stories.headline: Egypt orders independent news site Mada Masr to close
body: A Cairo court ordered Mada Masr, one of Egypt's last big independent outlets, to shut for running without a licence.
Editor Lina Attalah was fined about $53,400 and briefly detained.
She then learned of a one-year sentence passed in her absence in 2024; a retrial is set for 11 November.
stories.vc: Shrinking press freedom raises political risk ratings, which investors factor into Egypt's borrowing costs.

stories.headline: Sardinian restaurants ban phones at the family table
body: Fifteen restaurants in Sardinia will ask families to put away phones and tablets during meals.
The one-month pilot, called 'At the table without screens', is led by the island's children's ombudsman.
The aim is to get parents and kids talking while they eat.
stories.joke: Imagine: eye contact over pasta. Revolutionary.
stories.vc: 'Screen-free' is becoming a selling point; expect more cafés and brands to market it.

stories.headline: Melting Dolomites glaciers reveal 100-year-old war bombs
body: Retreating glaciers in Italy's Dolomites exposed a large cache of unexploded First World War bombs this summer.
The army removed and defused 250 explosives after hikers spotted them.
They date from the 1915–1918 'white war' between Austro-Hungarian and Italian troops.
stories.joke: Glaciers are melting so fast they're returning history's leftovers.
stories.vc: Visible climate effects like this keep pushing money into monitoring and adaptation tech.

stories.headline: Nairobi's 'Green Army' digs in before a record El Niño
body: Forecasters expect the strongest El Niño on record this winter, raising flood fears in Kenya's capital.
Teams of workers are clearing rivers and drains across Nairobi, a city of almost six million.
Floods in March killed more than 100 people in the city.
stories.vc: Cities preparing for climate shocks are a growing market for drainage, early warning and insurance tech.

stories.statLabel: on the DPDP Act for now
stories.headline: Supreme Court asks the Centre to respond on the publishers' DPDP plea
body: The Supreme Court sought the government's response to news publishers' challenge to the data protection law.
A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant refused to pause the law before hearing the government.
It issued notice on the publishers' request for a stay.
stories.joke: The court's verdict so far: 'Let's hear both sides.' Riveting.
stories.vc: Until the court rules, companies have to keep preparing for the DPDP rules that kick in from May 2027.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty end flat, but small caps rise 2%
body: The Sensex ended 8 points lower on Tuesday and the Nifty slipped 3 points to 22,749.
Bharti Airtel, Trent and Maruti gained, while Axis Bank, TCS and Asian Paints fell.
The midcap index rose about 1% and the smallcap index about 2%.
stories.joke: A whole day of trading to move 8 points. Peak efficiency.
stories.vc: Small caps beating the big indices shows retail risk appetite is strong, helpful for upcoming IPOs.

stories.headline: IndiaMART's quarterly profit rises 10%
body: IndiaMART's September-quarter profit rose 9.8% to ₹90.7 crore, and revenue grew 10% to ₹428.6 crore.
Profit fell 47% from the previous quarter.
Its shares closed 4% higher at ₹1,625.95.
stories.joke: B2B: boring to business, beautiful to shareholders.
stories.vc: Steady, profitable B2B marketplaces are getting a fresh look as consumer tech burns cash.

stories.headline: Simplismart raises $14M, with NVIDIA joining, to cut AI running costs
body: AI infrastructure startup Simplismart raised $14 million led by Dallas Venture Capital, with NVIDIA and Accel joining.
Its platform helps companies run AI models more cheaply at scale.
It plans to expand in North America and work with cloud and sovereign AI partners.
stories.joke: When NVIDIA invests in making AI cheaper, it's playing both sides of the table.
stories.vc: Inference optimisation is one area where Indian deep-tech startups can sell globally.

stories.headline: Practo co-founder's new startup Cent raises $15M
body: Cent, a preventive healthcare startup launched this year by Practo co-founder Shashank ND, raised $15 million.
Blume Ventures and South Park Commons led the round.
Cent also bought Medsee, an AI radiology startup.
stories.joke: Second startup, same founder, fewer doctor queues hopefully.
stories.vc: Repeat founders raise faster; preventive health is a bet that Indians will pay before they get sick.

stories.headline: Hennur–Bagalur road may get an elevated corridor
body: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda says Hennur–Bagalur Main Road could be made signal-free over five years or get an elevated corridor.
An elevated corridor is preferred, but only after a feasibility study.
He inspected ongoing roadworks on the stretch on Monday.
stories.joke: Bengaluru's two speeds: stuck and 'feasibility study'.
stories.vc: North Bengaluru's roads decide how fast the airport corridor fills with offices and homes.

stories.headline: Bengaluru bus drivers and traffic police show weaker lungs
body: A three-year study of over 10,000 Bengaluru frontline workers found reduced lung function.
It screened 4,517 BMTC drivers, 3,285 traffic police, 2,169 construction workers and 379 pourakarmikas.
All groups showed higher-than-normal early lung problems.
stories.vc: Air-quality data like this strengthens the case for electric buses and clean-air tech in Indian cities.

stories.headline: Google's Genie 4 builds playable worlds with sound
body: Google DeepMind released Genie 4, a 'world model' that generates interactive, realistic virtual worlds.
You can type prompts mid-simulation to change the scene, and it now makes matching audio.
Rivals are consolidating: AMD is buying World Labs and Amazon is in talks for Decart.
stories.joke: Finally, a game where you can rewrite the level when you're losing.
stories.vc: World models are a key training ground for robots and self-driving, which is why big tech is buying the startups.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic both claim AI refuted a big computer-science assumption
body: OpenAI released AI-made solutions to three long-standing maths problems, including a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis.
That hypothesis underpins how computer scientists judge which problems are hard to compute.
Hours after an Anthropic mathematician questioned OpenAI's work, Anthropic released its own refutation.
stories.joke: AI labs now compete on proofs. Mathematicians compete on reading them.
stories.vc: If AI can produce real research, labs gain a new story for valuations beyond chatbots.

stories.statLabel: parts from the US or allies
stories.headline: Anduril and Qualcomm plan a rugged US-made laptop
body: Anduril and Qualcomm announced BlueChip, a hardened laptop for the military, government and first responders.
About 90% of first-generation parts will come from the US or allied countries.
Pre-orders open in 2027.
stories.joke: Built to survive a war zone and, hopefully, a coffee spill.
stories.vc: Defence buyers will pay premiums for trusted supply chains, which opens doors for allied component makers, India included.

stories.headline: Ford's Fathom pickup can power a house
body: Ford's coming Fathom electric pickup will start at $28,350.
With new, cheaper chargers, it can send over 10 kW to a home.
That's enough to keep a fridge and air conditioner running for about half a day.
stories.joke: Power cut? Just plug the house into the truck.
stories.vc: Cheaper vehicle-to-home gear turns EVs into home batteries, a new angle for energy startups.

stories.headline: Bank of America tells customers not to give AI agents their passwords
body: Bank of America emailed customers asking them never to share log-ins with AI tools that act on their behalf.
More people are handing bank passwords to AI assistants.
That risks unwanted transactions, account lockouts or leaks if the assistant is hacked.
stories.joke: Your AI assistant is helpful. It does not need your PIN.
stories.vc: Banks will need safe ways to let AI agents act for customers, a big opening for fintech identity startups.

stories.headline: US warns hackers are exploiting critical PHP bugs
body: US cyber agency CISA says hackers are actively exploiting two critical bugs in PHP web software.
Federal agencies have three days to patch.
PHP reportedly runs about 70% of web-facing servers, and the bugs allow break-ins without passwords.
stories.joke: Update your software. Yes, today. Yes, you.
stories.vc: Every big bug wave lifts demand for patching and attack-surface monitoring tools.
